glassCss.quickSearchFailureMode:
REAL AND VERIFIABLE, in two forms.

(a) The workaround comment standing in current code — /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/shell/QuickSearch.module.css:11-18, verbatim:

/* Solid raised surface, NOT `composes: glass` (same S6/U8 rule
   Overlay.module.css's dialog/menu/popover chrome already follows, and the
   same --color-bg-raised recipe DatePicker's calendar popover uses —
   tokens.css: "modals, popovers, command palette"). The glass recipe was
   also visually broken here: this popover is a child of the topbar, whose
   own backdrop-filter forms a backdrop root, so the popover's blur could
   never sample the page behind it — the 86%-alpha chrome fill let page
   text/posters ghost through sharply under the results (2026-08-27 QA). */

(b) The commit that made the change — b07fe1a8b42b8981cebb84a1b5b27bebb8c61f90, "fix(web): visual QA sweep — clipping, overflow, and popover fixes at 380/768/1280", Thu Aug 27 17:51:40 2026, Oscar Chavez. Its body line: "QuickSearch popover switches from .glass (neutered under the topbar's backdrop root) to the raised-popover recipe". `git show b07fe1a -- apps/web/src/components/shell/QuickSearch.module.css` shows the diff removing `-  composes: glass from global;` from `.popover` and adding `+  background: var(--color-bg-raised);`, `+  border: 1px solid var(--color-border);`, `+  box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg);` (border-radius/padding/z-index were already present). `git log --all --oneline -S"composes: glass" -- apps/web/src/components/shell/QuickSearch.module.css` returns only `1e6a4f0 Loombre — initial public snapshot`, confirming the glass version shipped from the snapshot until b07fe1a removed it. Full file history: b07fe1a, 3a6f47a, 1e6a4f0.

MECHANISM, chased to the ancestor: QuickSearch is mounted inside the topbar (/Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/shell/QuickSearch.tsx:6 — "in a glass popover so search is reachable from any authenticated route"); the topbar is /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/shell/AppShell.module.css:43-56, setting `backdrop-filter: blur(14px)` at line 54. `.popover` is `position: absolute` (QuickSearch.module.css:20) inside `.container { position: relative }` (line 3), so it is a DOM descendant of that backdrop root. Result: the blur sampled the topbar's own composited output rather than the page, so nothing blurred while `--chrome-bg`'s 86% alpha stayed see-through — page text and posters read sharply through the results list.

CURRENT STATE after the fix (QuickSearch.module.css:19-35): `.popover` uses `background: var(--color-bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--color-border); box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg);` and composes nothing — which is why QuickSearch is NOT in the 10-consumer list.

playerControls.currentMobileBehavior:
At phone widths (<= 767.98px) exactly TWO things differ, one CSS and one JS. Everything else is byte-identical to desktop.

CSS (the only mobile CSS in the file) — PlayerControls.module.css:213-217 hides the volume slider: `.volumeSlider { display: none; }`. The mute toggle (PlayerControls.tsx:206-208) stays. Rationale recorded verbatim at 205-212: the transport cluster plus the 80px slider (~260px) plus the right icon cluster did not fit the bar's ~282px inner width at a 380px viewport — the fullscreen button spilled ~40px past the bar and 17px off the viewport (2026-08-27 QA; commit b07fe1a's "phone player bar drops the volume slider to stop viewport overflow").

JS — PlayerControls.tsx:132 `useMediaQuery("(max-width: 767.98px)")` gates ONLY the chapter surface: at 240-244 the anchored `.pickerPopover` renders when `chaptersOpen && !isPhone`; at 245-249 a `<BottomSheet open={chaptersOpen} onClose={…} title="Chapters">` renders when `isPhone`. The AUDIO/SUBTITLE track picker (253-279) is NOT gated — it stays an anchored `.pickerPopover` at every width, phones included. The inline comment at 233-239 states the sheet convention explicitly (README "Phone-only additions"; "an anchored popover has no sensible position against a full-width bottom control bar on a narrow viewport").

WHAT IS UNCHANGED at phone widths — i.e. what an LD-22 assertion block should pin, since re-declaring these changes nothing visually:
- `.bottomBar` (54-72): `position: absolute; left: var(--space-lg); right: var(--space-lg); bottom: var(--space-lg); z-index: 5; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-xs);` — a full-width-minus-gutters FLOATING bar, not edge-to-edge, with `border-radius: var(--radius-lg)`, its own `background: rgb(13 14 18 / 88%)` + `backdrop-filter: blur(18px)`, `box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg)`, `padding: var(--space-sm) var(--space-lg)`. No safe-area-inset handling.
- `.topBar` (12-26): `position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 5; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-sm); padding: var(--space-md) var(--space-lg);` plus the scrim gradient `linear-gradient(180deg, rgb(0 0 0 / 55%), transparent)`. No safe-area-inset (notch) handling.
- `.controlsRow` (126-130) keeps the three-zone centered layout: `.controlsSideLeft { flex: 1 }` (132-134), `.transportCluster { flex-shrink: 0 }` (136-141), `.controlsSideRight { flex: 1; justify-content: flex-end }` (143-149). There is NO `flex-wrap` anywhere — the row cannot wrap on a phone; it only fits because the slider is hidden.
- `.capabilityRow` (250-255) DOES have `flex-wrap: wrap`, so chips wrap on a phone and grow the bar's height.
- Control sizes stay desktop-sized: `.backButton` 38x38 (32-33), `.iconButton` 38x38 (158-159), `.playPauseButton` 46x46 (184-185).
- `.title` (95-103) keeps `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` — the PLAYER title still ellipsizes on a phone. This is not the item-detail file path; LD-18 does not reach it.
- `.pickerPopover` (222-234) is `position: absolute; bottom: calc(100% + var(--space-sm)); right: 0;` with no width cap — the track picker anchors to the bar's right edge at phone widths too.
- Visibility/motion (`.hidden` 82-85, `.topBar.hidden` 87-89, `.bottomBar.hidden` 91-93) is width-independent; auto-hide is driven by VideoPlayer's idle timer (PlayerControls.tsx:6-9).

LOCAL PLUGIN INFRASTRUCTURE: NONE EXISTS, for stylelint OR eslint. A find for eslint-rules / stylelint-rules / lint-rules / *-plugin directories outside node_modules returns nothing. /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/eslint.config.mjs uses only upstream `@eslint/js` + `typescript-eslint` plus BUILT-IN `no-restricted-globals` / `no-restricted-properties` — its playback-engine purity block (lines 24-61) is the repo's model for expressing a bespoke law through an off-the-shelf rule's config rather than a custom plugin.

HOW A CUSTOM STYLELINT RULE WOULD BE WIRED (all three pieces are new; nothing exists to extend):
- Write the plugin file, e.g. /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/stylelint-plugins/mobile-axis-reset.mjs, using `stylelint.createPlugin(ruleName, ruleFunction)`. It must be resolvable from apps/web (where stylelint is invoked and where .stylelintrc.json lives). ESM is fine — stylelint 17's Node API is ESM-only and the package graph is ESM throughout; repo script convention is `.mjs` with an SPDX header (`// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only`).
- Add `"plugins": ["./stylelint-plugins/mobile-axis-reset.mjs"]` to /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/.stylelintrc.json (paths in a JSON config resolve relative to the config file) plus the rule's own namespaced entry under `"rules"` (e.g. `"loombre/mobile-axis-reset": true`).
- NO script change is needed — apps/web/package.json:10's existing `stylelint "src/**/*.css"` picks up the config and therefore the plugin automatically, and gate.mjs:174 / ci.yml already run it.
- Placement caveat: keep the plugin file OUTSIDE `apps/web/src`, or `eslint src --max-warnings=0` will also lint it and `tsc --noEmit` may pull it in.
- Coverage caveat: the glob reaches only apps/web/src, so a plugin cannot police CSS anywhere else in the monorepo.

REPO-IDIOMATIC ALTERNATIVES, both already load-bearing and cheaper than a first-ever stylelint plugin — weigh these before writing one:
(a) A gate script under /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/scripts/, registered as a step in gate.mjs's `steps` array — the pattern of /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/scripts/grep-gates.mjs (registered at gate.mjs:180), which already carries five lettered sub-gates including one scoped to apps/web only (rule (e), "Forbids reading user-facing error copy off a `LoombreApiError` narrowing in apps/web (d4-e6)"). It exits non-zero printing `file:line: reason`.
(b) A CSS-text-parsing vitest test — the dominant idiom for CSS invariants here, precisely because jsdom evaluates no @media. Four live examples: /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/admin/settings/phosphor-mobile-css.test.ts (its `mobileBlock()` helper at 25-30 extracts the `@media (width <= 767.98px)` block by regex and asserts declarations inside it — the closest existing analogue to an LD-21 check); /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/ld14-mono-scale-conformance.test.ts (walks EVERY `*.module.css` under src/components with a real brace-matching parser at 28-60+, media-query-aware: "nested `{ ... }` bodies carved out, so a media-query wrapper … is judged on its OWN declarations, never its children's"); /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/player/controls-overlay-stacking.test.ts; /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/player/scrubber-hit-target.test.ts. Of these, ld14-mono-scale-conformance.test.ts is the only one that already walks the whole tree AND already understands media-query nesting — the nearest-fit skeleton for a repo-wide LD-21 check.

outOfScope: BRITTLE TEST REGEX — /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/admin/settings/phosphor-mobile-css.test.ts:27 uses `/@media \(width <= 767\.98px\) \{([\s\S]*)\}\s*$/` — greedy AND anchored to end-of-file.
